name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 17, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission
Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:01 p.m., on January 17, 2011, at
200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 14, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury (arrived at 5:20 p.m.)
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Leckness declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  January 17, 2011
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Musical Presentation by Tim Johnson, Producer of the Lord of the Strings

  Tim Johnson, Producer of the Lord of the Strings, demonstrated finger-style guitar and
  discussed upcoming Lord of the Strings programs.

P2.  Recognize the Saddleback Valley Black Wolverines, Jr. PeeWee Football Team for
  Placing Third in the Pop Warner National Championship in Florida and for
  Receiving a Sportsmanship Award

  Mayor Leckness presented Certificates of Commendation to members of the Saddleback
  Valley Black Wolverines.

P3.  Oath of Office for Newly Appointed Community Services Commissioners,
  Investment Advisory Commissioners, and Planning and Transportation
  Commissioners.

  City Clerk Karen Hamman administered the Oath of Office and presented Certificates of
  Appointment to Community Services Commissioners Edwin Althof, Wendy Bucknum,
  Sharon Campbell, John Maginnis, Brian Porter and Joyce Saltzgiver; Investment
  Advisory Commissioner Mazi Bahadori; and Planning and Transportation
  Commissioners Robert Bruchmann, Bill Ernisse and Steven Spillman. Commissioners
  Brian Skalsky, Peter Bastone, Dominic Nolan, and Rick Sandzimier were unable to
  attend the meeting and will receive their oath of office at a later date.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Dan Avery, M.V.: encouraged residents to read the new Patch blog and stated that they are doing
a very fair and honest job (http://missionviejo.patch.com/).

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 9, 11, and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

City Council Minutes  2  January 17, 2011
   Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated December 17, 2010, in the amount of $836,159.34

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated December 24, 2010, in the amount of $3,333,559.50

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2010

  Received and filed.

6.  Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2010

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2010

  Received and filed.

8.  Clarification of City Manager Employment Agreement (Section 5E)

  Approved the Seventh Amendment to the City Manager Employment Agreement.

10.  Orange County Transportation Authority 2010 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects: Renewed Measure M Regional Capacity
  Program

  (1) Adopted Resolution 11-07 Approving the Submittal of Candidate City of Mission
  Viejo Transportation Projects to the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)
  for Funding Consideration Under the OCTA Renewed Measure M Comprehensive
  Transportation Funding Program for Regional Capacity Projects; and (2) directed staff to
  transmit Resolution 11-07 to OCTA by January 28, 2011, in conjunction with the City’s
  funding applications for said projects.

12.  Fiber Communication and Traffic Controller Upgrade Project - Various Locations
  (CIP 797)

  (1) Awarded the construction contract for the base bid in the amount of $348,800 to
  Crosstown Electrical & Data, Inc., for the subject project; (2) authorized staff to re-bid
  the additive bid portion of the project as a separate contract.

City Council Minutes  3  January 17, 2011
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

14.  Appointment of City Commission Members

  Council Member Reardon announced that she has asked Commissioner Schweinberg to
  remain on the Planning and Transportation Commission until her proposed nominee is
  available on March 1, 2011.

  Council Member Schlicht advised the Council that Mark Dobrilovic has agreed to
  continue serving on the Investment Advisory Commission until the person she wishes to
  nominate has returned from vacation.

  Motion made by Mayor Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to appoint Scott
  Whelchel to the Investment Advisory Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht requested that the Thomas Paine quote she read at the last
  meeting be included in the Minutes. She also noted that she felt Council Member Ury’s
  Council Comments were incomplete.

  Council Member Ury indicated that he is very comfortable with the way his comments
  are summarized in the Minutes.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve
  the Minutes for the regular meeting of January 3, 2011, as amended.

  Amendment to January 3, 2011, Minutes: include the Thomas Paine quote which Council
  Member Schlicht read as part of her Council Comments.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  4  January 17, 2011
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

9.  Memorandum of Understanding  for  the  El  Toro  Road  Traffic  Light
  Synchronization Program

  Council Member Schlicht requested that staff to talk to the Transportation Committee
  about reconsideration of unprotected left-hand turn lanes as they work on the El Toro
  Road synchronization program.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to approve
  the Memorandum of Understanding C-0-1692 with the Orange County Transportation
  Authority for the El Toro Road Traffic Light Synchronization Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

11.  Montanoso Drive Neighborhood Traffic Management Program Phase 2 (CIP 779)

  Director Public Works Mark Chagnon discussed the questions that Council Member
  Reardon posed to him before the meeting and he outlined his responses regarding the
  Montanoso Drive Phase 1 traffic calming objectives.

  The following expressed opposition to the proposed Phase 2 improvements on
  Montanoso Drive: Debra Stanley, M.V. and Judy Smoke, M.V.

  The following expressed support for the Phase 2 project: Jim Grissom, M.V. and Wendy
  Bucknum, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) award
  the construction contract for the subject project to Kormx, Inc., in the amount of
  $188,100; (2) adopt Resolution 11-08 Amending the Fiscal Year 2010-2011 Budget for
  Costs Related to Montanoso Drive Neighborhood Traffic Management Program, Phase 2
  (CIP 779).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  5  January 17, 2011
 13.  Update on the Department of Energy EECBG and Solar Photovoltaic Panel System,
  City Hall (CIP 320), and Options for Using the Balance of the Grant Funds

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the possibility of using the grant funds for
  installation of solar-powered driver feedback or radar signs.

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay announced that the city would probably lose the
  grant funds with the time it takes to get approval from the Department of Energy
  therefore he recommends proceeding with the proposed spending plan.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, to approve
  staff recommendation to spend the balance of the Department of Energy EECBG (Energy
  Efficient Block Grant) funds on the replacement of existing metal halide parking lot light
  fixtures with induction lighting at the Civic Center and the Community Center, high
  pressure sodium security lights at the Community Center with LEDs, and yellow
  incandescent lights with LEDs in City traffic signals.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

16.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented the report.

17.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

18.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney’s Report

City Council Minutes  6  January 17, 2011
 19.  Review of CUSD Settlement Agreement

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented a brief overview of the CUSD litigation and
  settlement agreement.

City Manager’s Report

Council Member Schlicht inquired about the process for minute-taking since closed session
proceedings are no longer recorded. City Attorney Curley announced that he will keep a
confidential minute book and will hand-record any action that is taken in closed session.

Council Member Schlicht asked about the retention of the closed session audio recordings. City
Attorney Curley responded that in accordance with the resolution adopted by the City Council at
the last meeting and the city’s normal policy, the tapes will be retained for two years.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley expressed her condolences to Director of Library Services Valerie
Maginnis who recently lost her son in a tragic accident. She commended city staff for
organizing a very successful whooping cough vaccination clinic and she thanked resident Anna
T. Boyce for helping as well. Council Member Kelley announced that Mission Viejo has its own
celebrity football player, Mark Sanchez, a graduate of Mission Viejo High School. Mark is now
a member of the Jets and she congratulated the team on their victory against the Patriots. She
also discussed the fine work of the Mission Viejo Elks who recently gave 4,400 dictionaries to
all of the 3rd graders in Saddleback Valley. She noted that the Elks are an outstanding group and
they do so much for the community by raising money for scholarships, children, seniors and
veterans. Council Member Kelley announced that the city will sponsor a cardiac screening
program at Montanoso Recreation Center from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on January 22 and from
4:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on January 26, 2011. The screening is valued at $1,500 and is available
for an $85 tax-deductible donation. The test is the best tool for detection of the risks of sudden
cardiac death and is open to anyone age 5 and over in Mission Viejo and beyond. Council
Member Kelley thanked staff member Denise Matson for bringing this to the attention of the city
and helping to organize the event. She also discussed her attendance at a Martin Luther King
birthday celebration at Mission Viejo Christian Church and she commended the Pastor and the
congregation for bringing together communities and speakers to recognize a man of vision who
changed life in our nation. Council Member Kelley concluded her comments by announcing that
the Community of Character word for the month of January is perseverance.

City Council Minutes  7  January 17, 2011
 Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon thanked staff and Council Member Kelley for organizing the
whooping cough clinic. She and several of the Sunday school teachers from her church took
advantage of the opportunity and received a vaccine. She also discussed her recent visit to the
Meat House on Alicia Parkway and she encouraged residents to make a trip to this great new
local store. Council Member Reardon announced that she and Council Member Schlicht were
asked to speak at the Casta del Sol Democratic Club and she thanked them for the inclusive
invitation since she and Ms. Schlicht are both registered Republicans. She also announced that
she was invited to judge a National Speech and Debate Tournament at Concordia University with
over 500 home-schooled high school students from 13 states. She noted that Mission Viejo has a
fairly significant home school population as well. After spending the day judging these debates,
Council Member Reardon expressed confidence that many young people are learning to deal
with the fear of public speaking. She announced that she also had the pleasure of attending the
swearing-in ceremony for County Supervisors Pat Bates, John Moorlach and Shawn Nelson.
Council Member Reardon expressed her condolences to Valerie Maginnis who recently lost her
son in a tragic accident and to her friends, the Sickles, whose son was killed on New Year’s Eve.
Finally, she sent well wishes to her friend, a young boy, who spent six hours in surgery today for
the removal of a brain tumor and she asked everyone to keep the boy and his family in their
thoughts and prayers.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that she was fortunate to watch Mark Sanchez win many
football championships in Mission Viejo. She has always been a Jets fan so she is happy that
Mark is having a fabulous season playing for the Jets and she is looking forward to the Super
Bowl. Council Member Schlicht thanked Brad Morton for posting a blog article about another
cougar sighting in the city and she noted that these cats are ambush predators so residents should
remain aware and cautious. She thanked the Casta del Sol Democratic Club for the invitation to
speak at their recent meeting and she announced that she visited the new Meat House store and
she encourages residents to do the same. Council Member Schlicht read a quote from the
Reverend Dr. Martin Luther King: “Nothing in the world is more dangerous than sincere
ignorance and conscientious stupidity.” She noted that Dr. King brought hope and opportunity
for people to work together and he did change the world.

Mayor Pro Tem Ury
21.  Affordable Housing Options for Mission Viejo Workers

  Mayor Pro Tem Ury presented his report.

  Dan Avery, M.V.: announced that he is glad to see the Council taking a leadership role in
  this regard. He stated that affordable housing issues have been handled poorly by state
  governments and it is an excellent idea to investigate housing options for those providing
  a needed and productive service to the community.

City Council Minutes  8  January 17, 2011
   Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct
  staff to explore options regarding Affordable Housing and its ability to be prioritized for
  those working in Mission Viejo.

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

Council Member Ury stated that the Council Member’s hearts and prayers go out to Valerie
Maginnis and her family, and the entire community is with Valerie and praying for her.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Leckness announced that Saturday was a great day in Mission Viejo. It began with
Debbie Reynolds’ appearance at the Murray Center. KSBR assembled a fantastic setting and
interviewed Ms. Reynolds for an hour. She spoke about her life and it was a really great time for
all who attended. Later that day, Mayor Leckness visited the Meat House and he encouraged
residents to stop by the new store. Finally, that evening, he attended the Lord of the Strings
concert and he noted that it was a first class ending to a terrific day in Mission Viejo.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Scott Meyer, to Monday, February 7,
2011, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 7, 2011

City Council Minutes  9  January 17, 2011
